name: Ping
description: A star 65 parsecs away, 40 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 23685: radius 40.184 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 405.563 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.062) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 23685: effective temperature 4089 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.052)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 1.75 from 2024A&A...690A..97C; the 8 published values span log g 1.45 to 1.88, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 23685: distance 65.402 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.012), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 65 parsecs away, 40 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 406 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,089 K, so 40.184 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 23685: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Epsilon Leporis
quotes.card: Epsilon Leporis, Latinized from ε Leporis, formally named Ping, is a third-magnitude star in the southern constellation Lepus.
quotes.introduction: The apparent visual magnitude of +3.166 places it third in brightness among the stars in this constellation.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 2962546605447869184 (quality A), from 2018A&A...616A...7S; Gaia DR3 measures none
